questions.question: What was the Three-Fifths Compromise in the US Constitution?
options: Enslaved people were counted as three-fifths of a person for representation, giving slave states more power
Three-fifths of states had to approve laws
Taxes were set at three-fifths of income
questions.explanation: The 1787 Constitution counted enslaved people as 3/5 of a person for representation, strengthening slave states.

questions.question: What contradiction does Thomas Jefferson embody?
options: He wrote the Declaration of Independence proclaiming liberty while owning over 600 slaves
He opposed independence but signed the Declaration
He was British but became president
questions.explanation: Jefferson wrote that "all men are created equal" yet owned hundreds of slaves and never freed most of them.

questions.question: How does the US Constitution of 1787 treat slavery?
options: It never uses the word "slave" but protects slavery in several clauses
It banned slavery in the South only
It does not mention anything related to slavery
questions.explanation: The Constitution avoided the word "slave" while protecting slavery through the Three-Fifths Compromise and the Fugitive Slave Clause.

questions.question: Which period in American history came directly after the Civil War?
questions.explanation: The Civil War (1861-1865) was followed by Reconstruction (to 1877).

questions.question: When was the American colonial era?
questions.explanation: The Colonial Era ran from the founding of Jamestown in 1607 to the Declaration of Independence in 1776.
